The 2027 Fashion Retail CalendarHow to use this calendar
How to use

One Calendar, Four Layers, Zero Guesswork

Fashion runs on several clocks at once. Runways set trends months before shoppers see them, trade shows lock in what buyers will stock, and retail peaks decide when the money actually comes in. This calendar puts all of them together on one timeline for 2027, so buying, merchandising, marketing and e-commerce teams can plan from the same page.

LayerWhat it tells youWho uses it most
Fashion Weeks
Which trends and silhouettes will dominate the conversation
Content, social, merchandising
Collections
When each season should launch, peak and clear
Buying, merchandising, e-commerce
Trade Shows & Events
When buyers place orders and source materials
Buying, product, wholesale
Retail Moments
When demand peaks and what shoppers are looking for
Marketing, growth, e-commerce

How to read each date. Every entry shows the event, the period, the location when there is one, its status (Confirmed or Expected) and a one-line "why it matters" for anyone buying, selling or planning campaigns.

Three ways to get the most out of it:

  • Plan backward from the peak.Each month page includes a "Start planning" note, so you know which dates need two weeks of prep and which need three months.
  • Pick your battles.Not every date deserves a promotion. Use the big retail peaks for revenue, and the smaller moments for content, testing and brand building.
  • Plan the experience, not just the offer.Peak dates bring gift buyers, first-time visitors and shoppers stepping into new categories. They all hesitate at the same point: choosing a size. Each month flags where that hesitation spikes, so you can fix it before the traffic arrives.
Note: Dates marked Expected follow each organizer's usual window and may shift. Confirm before booking travel or locking media.

January

Clear Winter, Read the Returns, Set the Year's Trends

January runs on three tracks. Shoppers come back with gift cards and a reset mindset, Europe's regulated winter sales open, and the Fall/Winter 2027 menswear and couture shows start the trend conversation. It's also the month your holiday returns arrive, which makes it the best fit-data moment of the year.

Collections

Fall/Winter 2027

The men's and couture shows open the FW27 trend conversation that buyers will follow all season. In stores, the first Spring/Summer 2027 drops land next to clearance, which makes this a good moment for transitional pieces.

E-commerce tip

Your holiday returns are the best fit data you'll get all year. Pull return reasons by product and fix the worst offenders before Valentine's Day. Then add clear size guidance to clearance items, where shoppers tend to buy the size they can find instead of the one that fits.

Collections

Fall/Winter 2027 Runways

All four big womenswear weeks start within three weeks of each other, setting the references brands and buyers will work with for the rest of the year. Late in the month, the Spring/Summer 2027 launch begins as dresses and light jackets start replacing outerwear.

Late Feb
Spring/Summer 2027 main launch begins · GlobalDresses, light jackets and early swim start replacing outerwear
Expected
E-commerce tip

Valentine's Day falls on a Sunday, so Friday the 12th is your real delivery deadline. Put the order-by date on every product page, then switch to gift cards and express shipping once it passes. Gift buyers rarely know the recipient's size, so simple size guidance and easy exchanges help them go beyond a scarf.

March

Spring Arrives Early

Easter falls on March 28 in 2027, almost a month earlier than in 2026 (April 5 in 2026). That pulls pastel, occasion and family-outfit demand into March and squeezes the spring launch window. Paris closes the FW27 shows, and Mother's Day arrives first in the UK.

Swimwear and Resortwear

Swim and resort pieces start to move as the Northern Hemisphere warms up. At the same time, the Resort 2028 shows begin setting the travel-led trends that reach stores in November.

Late Apr

E-commerce tip

Returns are the Earth Day story most brands miss. Every return adds another round of shipping and handling, and some items never sell at full price again. Since most fashion returns come down to size and fit, helping shoppers choose right the first time is a sustainability move that also protects margin.

Fall/Winter 2027 Launch

The first knits and outerwear go live late in the month, right next to summer clearance. It's the moment to keep a full-price new-season story running while the sales do their job.

Late Jul–Aug
Fall/Winter 2027 launch begins · GlobalFirst knits and outerwear go live next to summer clearance

E-commerce tip

Use summer sales to clear stock, not to train shoppers to wait. Segment markdown emails by purchase history, and be clear about which sizes are left and how they fit. Clearance leaves stock in fringe sizes, and shoppers who settle for the size they can find become August returns.

Fall/Winter 2027 hits full launch, bringing the highest-value categories of the year. At the same time, the SS28 shows give you trend content months before those collections actually ship.

E-commerce tip

Fall is where fit matters most and returns cost the most. A coat one size too small can't be layered, and a narrow boot won't get worn. Shoppers spend more per item now, so they're more cautious. The more confident they feel about size and look, the more likely they buy instead of wishlisting.

Resort/Cruise

Resort pieces arrive in stores late in the month, giving vacation shoppers full-price newness in the middle of discount season.

Late Nov–Dec
Resort/Cruise collections in store · GlobalFull-price newness for vacation shoppers in the middle of discount season
Expected
E-commerce tip

Use Singles' Day as a dress rehearsal, then run Cyber Week in waves: early access, launch, reminder and last chance. Discount shoppers often order two or three sizes of the same item, so November looks strong and January takes it back. Helping them choose right the first time protects margin and core-size stock.

Quarterly planning

Your Quarter-Ahead Checklist

Run this checklist about eight weeks before each quarter starts. The first block repeats every quarter; the second covers what's specific to that quarter's peaks.

Q1Jan–Mar
Run it byEarly November
Peaks to prepareWinter sales, Valentine's Day, early Easter (Mar 28), UK Mothering Sunday
Quarter-specific checksClearance edits by size availability; gift guides that work when the buyer isn't the wearer; spring imagery shot by mid-February
Q2Apr–Jun
Run it byEarly February
Peaks to prepareMother's Day (four dates), Memorial Day, Father's Day, Prime Day, summer sales
Quarter-specific checksSwimwear fit content; one Mother's Day engine with per-market deadlines; a competing offer ready for Prime Day
Q3Jul–Sep
Run it byEarly May
Peaks to prepareSummer clearance, back to school, Labor Day, fall launch
Quarter-specific checksKidswear size guidance by age and height; fall outerwear and boot fit notes; SS28 runway content templates
Q4Oct–Dec
Run it byEarly August
Peaks to preparePrime Big Deal Days, Singles' Day, Black Friday to Cyber Monday, Christmas, Boxing Day
Quarter-specific checksStock depth in core sizes on hero products; site and fit tools stress-tested by mid-October; extended holiday return windows communicated clearly

The 2027 Fashion Retail CalendarQuarterly planning checklist
Checklist

Is Your Business Ready for the Next Quarter?

Use this checklist to review the key points of your operation's planning.

Q1January to March
  • Analyze last year's results.
  • Review inventory and plan winter sales.
  • Map trends and references for new collections.
  • Plan purchasing and restocking.
  • Organize campaigns for Valentine's Day, Presidents' Day and Easter.
Q2April to June
  • Prepare the launch and promotion of Spring/Summer collections.
  • Plan campaigns for Mother's Day, Father's Day and Memorial Day.
  • Review product and size performance.
  • Plan purchasing for Fall/Winter.
  • Evaluate opportunities for special launches.
Q3July to September
  • Plan sales and inventory renewal.
  • Prepare Fall/Winter launches.
  • Update storefronts and store content.
  • Plan campaigns for Back to School and Labor Day.
  • Start planning for Black Friday.
Q4October to December
  • Review inventory and size availability.
  • Organize campaigns for Black Friday, Cyber Week and Christmas.
  • Prepare your operation for a higher volume of orders.
  • Set holiday shipping cutoffs and return windows.
  • Analyze the year's results and plan for 2028.

Remember: planning isn't something you do just once. Track your results, revise your strategies and adapt the calendar to your business's needs.

Right size More conversion Fewer returns

The dates bring the traffic. Confidence closes the sale.

Every peak on this calendar brings shoppers who behave differently from your regulars: gift buyers guessing someone else's size, first-time visitors who've never worn your brand, and customers stepping into categories they buy once a year. Before they buy, they all ask the same question: will this fit me? When the answer is a guess, you see it as hesitation at checkout, abandoned carts, bracketed orders and a heavy returns month after every peak.

Sizebay gives shoppers a complete decision experience right on the product page. Size recommendation suggests the right size based on the shopper's body and on how each piece is actually cut, and virtual try-on lets them see how it will look before they add it to the cart. Together, they turn calendar traffic into confident purchases, so the sales your campaigns generate are sales you keep.

Plan the experience alongside the promotions, and 2027 will reward both.
